events.description: An engineer starts setting up multiple PostgreSQL servers in staging to try out pgpool-II for load balancing (infrastructure#259).
Prior to starting the work, the engineer takes an LVM snapshot of the production database and loads it into the staging environment, outside the normal automatic 01:00 UTC snapshot schedule.
GitLab.com experiences a sharp increase in database load, suspected to be spam; many users cannot post comments on issues and merge requests. Getting load under control takes several hours.
Part of the load is found to be caused by a background job trying to remove a GitLab employee's account and associated data, accidentally scheduled after the account was flagged for abuse.

Due to increased load, the PostgreSQL secondary's replication lags and fails because required WAL segments were already removed from the primary; WAL archiving was not in use, so the secondary must be manually re-synchronised.

An engineer wipes the secondary's data directory and runs pg_basebackup, which hangs silently; it later reports it cannot connect because max_wal_senders is exhausted. Engineers raise max_wal_senders from 3 to 32, and PostgreSQL fails to restart due to too many semaphores until max_connections is reduced from 8000 to 2000. pg_basebackup still hangs, and strace shows it blocked in a poll call.

An engineer suspects pg_basebackup left files in the secondary's data directory from previous attempts; it is later revealed this is normal behaviour (it waits silently for the primary to send data), which was not documented.

While trying to restore replication, an engineer wipes the PostgreSQL data directory believing it is the secondary, but it is the primary; about 300 GB of data is removed before the process is terminated a second or two after the mistake is noticed.

Engineers search for database backups and ask for help on Slack; both finding and using the backups fail completely. The pg_dump backups are missing because pg_dump 9.2 was used against PostgreSQL 9.6 and failed, and cron failure emails were rejected due to DMARC not being enabled.
A snapshot was created manually by an engineer (one of the two LVM snapshots available at the time of the outage).
The GitLab.com database is restored without webhooks, using the LVM snapshot from 6 hours before the outage with the copy process taking about 18 hours.
Final restoration procedures, including restoring webhooks and confirming operation, are completed.
